title: Titanium Fuel Pool Rack Spacer
function: Nuclear fuel storage rack spacer grid
alloyReason: Grade 2 CP-Ti (UNS R50400) is selected for Titanium Fuel Pool Rack Spacer where formability and corrosion resistance are prioritized over absolute strength. With 40% elongation and excellent weldability, Grade 2 CP-Ti forms a stable TiO₂ passive film that provides immunity to pitting in chloride environments up to 260°C. Its 345 MPa yield strength with 30% elongation makes it ideal for Nuclear fuel storage rack spacer grid requiring cold forming or bending without cracking. This rationale is driven by nuclear fuel storage rack spacer grid and specific design requirements.
process: Closed-die forging net shape for nuclear hardware geometry
CNC precision machining with SPC sampling
TIG welding all positions with SPC sampling
DPI dye penetrant inspect with SPC sampling
surfaceTreatment: Thermal oxidation 700C 2h in air to grow controlled 300nm TiO2 barrier layer for H2 permeation reduction — tailored for nuclear fuel storage application
commonFailures: Thermal ratcheting under cyclic temperature - controlled by stress-relief anneal 675C 2h Ar below beta-transus — critical for nuclear fuel storage performance

faq.q: What downhole temperature rating does Titanium Fuel Pool Rack Spacer have?
faq.a: Grade 2 CP-Ti maintains >90% of room-temperature tensile and yield strength at 200°C and >80% at 300°C. Titanium Fuel Pool Rack Spacer is suitable for nuclear fuel storage in geothermal (HDR/EGS) wells up to 300°C with appropriate consideration of creep in threaded connections. Above 300°C, dedicated creep testing per ASTM E139 is recommended for design life validation.

Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Fuel Pool Rack Spacer?
faq.a: Each Titanium Fuel Pool Rack Spacer shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for nuclear fuel storage.
